subject.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API

question: Should successful `after_compaction` hooks gain a supported current-session reset API, including native harness compactions, as a permanent plugin contract?
rationale: The capability is useful and narrower than the previously rejected arbitrary-key API, but accepting it commits OpenClaw to a state-mutating plugin surface spanning core, Gateway, Codex, Copilot, and external harness ownership boundaries.

options.title: Approve the narrow contract
options.body: Support `resetSession(reason?)` only on successful, unlocked after-compaction contexts with a core-owned deferred lifecycle queue, canonical key, stale guard, docs, and live proof.

options.title: Limit it to core compaction
options.body: Expose the API only on compaction paths where core already owns the full reset lifecycle, withholding it from native harness paths until a private bridge exists.

options.title: Keep resets internal
options.body: Decline the plugin API and solve recovery through an owner-controlled core or compaction-provider policy seam instead.

recommendation.title: Approve the narrow contract
recommendation.body: Support `resetSession(reason?)` only on successful, unlocked after-compaction contexts with a core-owned deferred lifecycle queue, canonical key, stale guard, docs, and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Their history spans the session reset and pre-compaction lifecycle that defines the permanent ownership boundary for this API.
